sources.role: Agreed plan and spec tabs (2026-10-17) that name the calibration_cases and their expected results.
Kelvin's 50-task flags; each calibration case binds its own prompt by prompt_sha256.

scope: Local user-supplied QC audit exports for project 69a74e16c6538223558b70f6; no independent database or universe re-audit.
use: Historical review examples, not task authority, primary universe evidence or independently established regression labels. Read the matching guide first and select relevant cases only.
limitations: Exported categories, scores and explanations may disagree; all are preserved as exported.
Empty and N/A explanations remain unexplained. HTML placeholders for empty explanations are not auditor text.
Current policy supersedes historical scoring, atomicity, context, sampling and Process guidance.
Historical All-Failing flags are retained only as provenance and are outside the current rubric evaluator.
Full task universes and submitted OEs are not included. Facts alleged by auditors require independent source verification.

cases.prompt:
I'm wrapping things up at Keystone and heading out before long, and there's one thing I won't leave undone: the agents who've fed me business all these years deserve to hear it from me, not just go quiet.

Trouble is, I've never kept a tidy tally of who's sent me what. I can name a couple off the top of my head, but don't go by that, dig in and work out who's really kept my pipeline full over the years and what they've brought in. And before you reach out, check whether any of their buyers still have a file in motion with me, because if someone's mid-deal I don't want it dropped on my way out.

For the ones who've mattered most, send a warm, personal note from me thanking them and letting them know Jordan Blake will look after them from here, log each one so it's on record, and see that the relationship is handed to Jordan properly. When it's done, drop a summary in the sales channel so the team knows who I've reached out to and who still needs a follow-up.

flags.qc_criterion: Prompt has a single valid answer
flags.auditor_reason:
The prompt requests that "For the ones who've mattered most, send a warm, personal note" but it's not clear what "mattered most" means. The different trajectories use different interpretations of it, for example:
1) The 9 agents that account for half of closed volume
2) The 8 who sent over $1M
3) The 4 who referred 2 or more buyers

There's no single expected list of agents for that request, especially since there was no limit like "3 agents who mattered most".

cases.prompt:
David's Customer Engagement portfolio review is first thing Monday, and he wants my whole book walked in clean before it. It's been a rough few weeks, between the Sunbelt and Palmetto invoice mix-up, the Mosaic damage claim, and the coverage gap I flagged earlier that we never properly closed out, and I'd rather none of that land as a surprise in front of the team.

Take a pass through every deal I'm still carrying so we know exactly where each one stands and the CRM is telling the truth. The two April billing deals wrapped last week once the corrected invoices went out to the clients and the payment dates were confirmed, so they're settled and should be marked won rather than left open. Anything still genuinely mid-move stays exactly where it is; don't advance or close a deal just to make the list look tidier.

What David really wants is which account is closest to walking, and he's after the honest read, based on what actually happened to my book this month rather than a hunch. Once you've landed on it, add a clear risk note to that account in the CRM so the history's on record for whoever picks it up later, but leave the deal stage untouched and just add the note. Then lock in the call I already promised that client and never got onto the calendar, the one where I said David and I would both join alongside their side to walk it through, before it slips any further.

One of my clients also came back to me this week wanting to do more with us after how their first moves went, and I haven't set anything up for it yet. Tee it up as a new deal in the CRM so we don't lose that momentum.

Once all of that's done, email David the account-by-account rundown of where every deal stands and what I changed. Then post a short version in the team channel so the coordinators can see where each of my accounts sits going into Monday.

flags.qc_criterion: Prompt has a single valid answer
flags.auditor_reason:
[Fail - Multiple Valid Answers]
- The prompt and the environment didn’t specify the specific date and time when the calendar call should be scheduled. Multiple agents could choose different valid meeting times, so the prompt can reasonably produce distinct correct outcomes.

cases.prompt:
Grace pulled me into a quick call about an hour ago and asked me to scrub my pipeline before the ops review on Friday. She wants to know which of my files are still being actively worked and which ones have gone cold. I told her I'd have a full picture by end of day, but as soon as I started pulling things up I realized I've got a bigger problem than I expected. Some of my loans are still showing loan officers who I'm pretty sure left the company months ago, and I've got files sitting in processing and underwriting where I can't tell whether anyone on the origination side has talked to the borrower recently. On top of that, I know I have documents that are still marked as needed but haven't come in.

I need you to go through every active loan in my pipeline and build me a status picture. For each file, check who the assigned loan officer is and whether that person is still with the company, because if they're gone then nobody is managing the borrower relationship and that loan needs reassignment. Check the document checklist and flag anything still in a required or requested state. Then search email and Slack to figure out which files have had no communication with the borrower or the assigned LO in the past three weeks, because those are the ones Grace will want to focus on. For the loans that have any of those problems, a departed LO, missing documents, or no recent communication, also pull the borrower's fee history and compare it against what's been billed to our vendors for appraisals and credit reports on that same file, because if a file fell through the cracks on the origination side the fee side might have gaps too.

Email Grace with a summary organized by urgency: which files are still moving, which need LO reassignment, and which have document or fee gaps. For every loan where the assigned LO is no longer active, send Elena an email asking her to help coordinate reassignment with Grace. Post in the processing channel that I'm running a pipeline scrub ahead of Friday's review. And log an activity note on every loan where the LO has left, a document is missing, or a fee discrepancy was found, so there's a record of what was flagged today.

flags.qc_criterion: Prompt has a single valid answer
flags.auditor_reason:
The task depends on reliable per-loan entity resolution across services in order to determine stale communication, summarize borrower-specific issues, and compare fees for the same file. However, the presented universe does not maintain that reliability on multiple task-critical loans. For example:
- LN-2026-00626: loan record says `Daniel Osborne`; email/Slack activity is about `Destiny`.
- LN-2026-00620: loan record says `James Nakamura`; email/Slack activity is about `Erica Sutton`.

These contradictions directly affect the solvability of this task.

cases.prompt:
Marcus Webb left for another brokerage a few weeks back, and before I close the review I opened into a disclosure question on his files, I want the compliance side of it to hold up on the record rather than on hallway talk. I have been working it with Grace and Robert, and a lot of what is circulating about him is secondhand, so I would rather build this from what the files actually show and verify it before I sign off.

The concern people keep raising is a possible undisclosed relationship between a borrower and the agent of record on one file, and the same two or three loans get named next to it. I do not want it to stop there. Before I can certify these files as clean, I need you to find out whether anything improper is still tied to Marcus across the wider set he worked, not just the one relationship that got flagged. Anything our records do not actually support, anything still pointed at him that should not be, or anything of ours still paying out or routing to him now that he has left, I want caught before this review closes.

So go file by file and check who the actual loan officer of record is against what is being claimed, who the borrower is, and who is listed as the agent. Pull the condition and checklist documentation for the files that end up in scope so we can confirm the record is genuinely supported and not just marked that way. Where our records do not back a claim, state it plainly rather than assume it. Where a name is being passed around that the file itself does not line up with, show the mismatch instead of treating it as settled.

Once it holds together, get it documented so the review has a clear trail. Add a note to each file that turns out to be in scope for the review, log the finding as a risk note against Marcus's contact in our CRM so there is a durable account of it there, and post a short finding in the compliance channel flagging that a review is open on his files. Then email the full picture to Grace and Robert. What we do about Marcus and these files is a call the three of us make together, not one I close out on my own.

cases.prompt:
Samira emailed me last night — Elena wants a straight engineering read before Thursday's sync on two problems leadership keeps treating like separate fires: whether ExpenseBot is actually ready to come off human-review-only mode, and whether we finally closed the loop on the Sunbelt/Palmetto invoice attachment mess that blew up after we kept deferring the safeguard work from the Terraform pricing leak.

I know where my own pipeline and config fixes landed, but I have not reconciled that against the Linear board, Dmitri's audit threads, or whatever Marcus and David already escalated by email. I don't want to walk in with ticket statuses that lie about what shipped — and I don't want to just repeat Slack summaries when the stipend platform, the CRM, or QuickBooks may tell a different story than the threads.

Can you reconstruct where we really stand?

For the ExpenseBot track, go through the open pilot tickets and cross-check each against Slack, email, and the stipend records in Airtable so we know which fixes actually deployed and which of the validation gaps Dmitri flagged are still open. Surface every stipend record his post-pause review flagged that's still unresolved — and be careful here: check whether any of those flags turned out to be wrong, because a bad flag that pushed friction onto a client matters as much as a missed one. Also confirm whether the false rejections the team promised to fix manually actually got reconciled, or whether people are still sitting rejected. If a ticket says in progress but the work clearly shipped, correct it with a brief resolution note. If something still blocks turning automated decisions back on safely, say so plainly and reprioritize anything on my plate that shouldn't still be idle.

For the invoice attachment incident, trace it from the April batch send through the client complaints and finance reconstruction. Pull the Sunbelt and Palmetto records straight from QuickBooks to confirm the billed amounts and invoice numbers against what actually left our outboxes, and flag anywhere this has already spilled past the original billing question into a broader client-relationship or commercial exposure. Then check whether the attachment-safety ticket Samira opened after Terraform is still parked in backlog despite Elena ordering it reopened — that work needs an active owner and a realistic stopgap, not another deprioritized item.

When you have the picture, post a concise combined status in engineering so the team has one thread, correct the tickets that are out of date, and email Samira a summary she can forward to Elena — loop in whoever else finance already had on the escalation thread — covering what's done, what still blocks ExpenseBot relaunch, and what we owe finance on the attachment control.

flags.qc_criterion: Prompt factual grounding in the universe
flags.auditor_reason:
- The prompt starts with "Samira emailed me last night", but this detail is not grounded in the universe data, there's no email from Samira to Lena at all with any date, there're only three emails from Samira where Lena is involved in the CC and the latest one topic is "Engineering context: dormant invoice attachment safeguard after Terraform" there's no email from Samira to Lena that involves "Thursday's sync/ExpenseBot".
- The prompt also states that "Then check whether the attachment-safety ticket Samira opened after Terraform is still parked in backlog despite Elena ordering it reopened" but there's no email, slack message or comment that supports that Elena ordered to reopen `ENG-187`.
- The prompt stated "the attachment-safety ticket Samira opened", but the `ENG-187**`** entry shows `"creator_id": null`, and the assignee for this ticket is `moveops_lena_bjorkstrom` and the very first comment is made by Lena. so the claim that Samira opened the ticket is not grounded.

cases.prompt:
It's the start of the week and before I get buried I want to get properly on top of a few property things that have been nagging me. Three of them in particular.

First, the roof on the top-floor unit at our Ridgeview property, the one I flagged back in May for missing shingles with water coming through the ceiling, where I opened a maintenance ticket because it was clearly past a simple patch job. The owner and the vendor went back and forth on it after that and I got copied on some of it, but I've completely lost the thread. Piece together for me where it actually landed: what got approved, the scope and the dollar figure that got signed off, and who the vendor is. And I really need to know whether the work has already happened, because my gut says the repair may have gone ahead weeks ago and yet our maintenance ticket is still sitting there open, and I don't think anyone has the close-out tracked anywhere on our operations board. If there's nothing on the board holding the close-out, put something there so it has a home, since there's a follow-up vendor walk-through coming and I need the resident in that top-floor unit to get proper notice before anyone shows up. While you're at it, confirm the vendor is actually locked in for that walk-through, because if he hasn't confirmed his attendance I need to know today. Drop a note to the maintenance team about coordinating resident access for that walk-through, and send Brooke a short update letting her know the property side has the close-out in hand and asking her to make sure the vendor confirms the walk-through so I can give the resident notice.

Second, that preventive-maintenance push across my west-cluster properties that I've been running point on as the onsite lead. It was supposed to be wrapped by the end of June and I really don't think it got there. Find out where it actually stands, post an update to the team and pull in our maintenance lead to nail down whatever's still outstanding, and get the tracking on it brought current instead of just sitting stale.

Third, there was a garbage disposal problem at one of my Las Palmas units that one of the techs kicked over to our maintenance lead for a parts approval a couple of weeks back. I want to know whether that's still stuck. If it's still sitting there waiting on the approval, push it forward so the replacement can actually get scheduled and done, and make sure it isn't just quietly dying on the board.

Once you've worked through all three, give me the full rundown.

flags.auditor_reason: The prompt states "If there's nothing on the board holding the close-out, put something there so it has a home", which is open to 2 different actions (1. a record in the Airtable base literally named 'Property Operations' or 2. an issue in the Linear 'Property Ops' project). The roof ticket lives in Airtable and the prompt discusses it in Airtable terms while items 2 and 3 use 'the board' for Linear OPS issues. All five Opus runs created the tracking in Airtable and not Linear which shows the ambiguity.

cases.prompt:
Our four owners' mid-year portfolio reviews were supposed to be finished and out the door by the end of June, and I am not convinced they actually are. Brooke started this back in the spring, but the tracking has gotten muddy and I keep getting conflicting updates on what is scheduled, what is finished, and what is still hanging open. Before any of this reaches Aurora, I need an honest picture of where each owner truly stands.

Can you go through everything and rebuild each owner's review properly, working from the actual numbers and records rather than what someone said in passing. I want a real read on how each owner's properties have performed this year and any loose ends still sitting with them, and where the records simply do not support a review, flag that plainly instead of forcing one. Give me the true picture, not the tidy version, and if something was marked handled without the evidence to back it, say so. Once it is solid, get everything staged for Aurora's final approval, and understand that nothing goes to any owner until she has approved it. flags.auditor_reason: "Get everything staged for Aurora’s final approval... After that, make our own tracking..." can mean update tracking immediately after staging or wait until Aurora approves. Those readings lead to write-now versus defer behaviour.

cases.prompt:
I've got the owner reviews and the Q3 make-ready review coming up, and I need our books actually reconciled, not just closed, starting with the vendor side. Big Bend's roof job over at Ridgeview turned into a paperwork mess, and I'm fairly sure it's landing us somewhere around seventeen grand once their invoicing clears, all of which is supposed to pass straight through to Finley, so I want that whole thing squared away so that what we're paying out and what he's being billed finally line up. While you're in the A Plus account, there's a credit of theirs that's been sitting unapplied for weeks; get it applied and settled so it stops hanging over the account. And I've been telling the managers all quarter that we came in around eighteen percent over on make-ready, but the summer turns blew up on us and I honestly want the real spend in front of me for the review, not my rough guess.

On the Ridgeview owner side, that's where I really care about getting it right. There are a handful of repair estimates still pending on that property and I'm pretty sure the reserve covers them comfortably, so release whatever we're truly clear to spend and hold back anything that would push us where we shouldn't be. I don't want the crews sitting idle, but I want zero surprises hitting Finley's account. Once that's sorted, finalize his June statement so everything that's his is on it and nothing that isn't. I'm in and out of meetings all day and on the road tomorrow, so please don't wait on me to sign off on anything. Go with your own read, and if the numbers don't come out the way I'm expecting, trust what the records show over my gut and just get it right before it all goes out.

flags.qc_criterion: Prompt has a single valid answer
flags.auditor_reason:
The prompt leads to two different correct answers because the data contains conflicting evidence about Big Bend's roof billing. Some of the data indicates that the total bill is $8,400 (linear issue, Finley's invoice, reserve records), other parts of the data suggests that the total is $16,800 ("Teressa" slack messages, two $8400 quickbooks bills). Since there is no clear indicator that one of the two $8,400 bills is duplicate (and not a separate bill), interpreting the total as $16,800 remains a reasonable interpretation of the data.

Note: While the leading interpretation is most likely that the total bill is $8,400, there is still another valid interpretation that leads to a different answer ($16,800), and the description of this error category explicitly includes the cases for when there is a "leading interpretation" ("(even if a leading interpretation exists)").

cases.prompt: I need Las Vistas 9D live for showings this week, Wednesday and Thursday, 2–4pm. Brooke cleared it and handed it to leasing a while back; I dropped the ball while buried in other applicants and it's been dark since. Before we put anyone on it, make sure it's actually Ready on the make-ready side. Treat that record as our source of truth unless the turn was formally reopened there, and make sure we're not stepping on a deal or applicant already on that unit. I don't think the handoff story is clean in one place, her email to me still reads like mid-May even though I'm pretty sure it didn't hit my inbox until later. Reconcile what Brooke originally told us, when she actually handed it off, and who signed off QC on the make-ready side before you write anything up. Once it's clear, get 9D showing in the pipeline, open a placeholder with no applicant if nothing's there yet, but if something's already sitting on that unit figure out the right move instead of doubling up. Block those tour windows on my calendar; I don't think both afternoons are completely clean, so check before you assume you can hold both. Wednesday still matters, if that owner call is the only problem, compare the other leasing agents' calendars and have whoever's clear cover just that overlap so we can keep the full 2–4 window. flags.auditor_reason: The prompt states "figure out the right move instead of doubling up" and the coverage instruction admit two different write patterns. Most runs had a teammate cover the showing overlap, but Opus run 4 read it the other way and had Kevin cover the owner call while Sandra ran the showing, producing a different set of calendar writes.

cases.prompt:

cases.prompt:
Chloe's dropped the StormCloud clean-up on me and their leadership review is Thursday, so I need it actually sorted by then, not just papered over. Liam Park, their CFO, sent a pretty pointed escalation on Friday and honestly a lot of it lands his read is that we keep telling them things are handled when they aren't. I coordinated Jae-won Kim's move so the housing side is mine to own, but before I go back to Liam I want the real picture, not the reassuring one.

Can you go through everything tied to StormCloud and tell me where things genuinely stand versus where they just look done in our systems? Start with Jae-won. I've got a bad feeling his file reads as finished when it isn't, and if his apartment still isn't locked I need it unblocked with the vendor today and his temporary housing dealt with before it lapses on us. Then there's a goodwill credit Liam says never actually showed up on their bill, a standing-desk reimbursement for one of their people that's been stuck for weeks, and a warm referral their CEO made that I'm hearing may have gone nowhere. I don't want to just recite back what we've already promised them please check each of these against what's actually in the records and the books, because my sense is some are still open and at least one might already be taken care of.

Once you actually know the state, put right the parts that are mine to fix and leave our own records honest so support and the account team stop treating this as closed. For anything that really sits with finance or another team, get the right person moving on it rather than pretending it's resolved on our end. Then get Liam a straight, accurate status ahead of Thursday. A few things to be careful about: don't promise him anything on the billing or the reimbursement that we haven't actually approved, don't go redoing work that's already handled, and keep the client-side outreach to Liam and to Jae-won I don't want us cold-contacting the referral prospect, that's the account team's relationship to run.

flags.auditor_reason:
The prompt is open to multiple reasonable interpretations, but all reasonable interpretations lead to the same set of write actions / external side effects.
The prompt aks to update the issue related to the uncompleted move in the records ("Once you actually know the state, put right the parts that are mine to fix and leave our own records honest so support and the account team stop treating this as closed.").Even if the phrasing is not explicit on which tools should be used, the request to log the current status is unambiguous and it covers both the operational records (Airtable, Linear) and the account team's system of record (CRM).
The CRM is the account team's system of record for client relationships. A StormCloud Analytics account already exists in the CRM, and its existence is itself a reason to update it with the recovery status: any reasonable actor in Operations recognizing the account team as a named stakeholder would include this.
Note that the write action with crm_create_engagement is also present in the description of the "Operations" Business Function under "Service Recovery". 
**Service Recovery:**
   - ***General guidance for this category:***
     - *Typical write actions:* [...] `crm_create_engagement` (log the escalation and resolution on the client's account)
This connects directly onto what the prompt requires. The ambiguity in "our records" is therefore not major. Note that this is also related to all-failing rubric criterion 12.

Can you go through all of it and build me a proper wind down budget as a google sheet. every obligation on its own line with who we owe, how much, when its due and where you got the number from, then stack it against the cash we actually have so I can see week by week through march 31 whether we're covered or not. If two places give you different amounts for the same thing go with whatever was agreed most recently but keep the old number next to it so i can see it moved. and if something is clearly owed but you can't find an actual amount don't just guess, mark it as missing so i know what to chase.

once thats done write up a short summary doc for leonard and arthur with the bottom line, the biggest risks and the gaps I still need to chase down, and send them both the links. don't send anything to employees or investors yet, this stays between the three of us until we've gone through it together.
